makaleler.baslik_en: Prenatal exposure to drug treatment for attention deficit/hyperactivity disorder and risk of neurodevelopmental disorders: Scandinavian multinational cohort study.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Prenatal exposure to drug treatment for attention deficit/hyperactivity disorder and risk of neurodevelopmental disorders: Scandinavian multinational cohort study.
makaleler.ozet_en: OBJECTIVE: To assess whether prenatal exposure to drug treatment for attention deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD) increases the risk of neurodevelopmental disorders in children. DESIGN: Population based cohort study. SETTING: Nationwide register data on births, dispensed drugs, and specialist healthcare diagnoses from Denmark, Norway, and Sweden. PARTICIPANTS: 3 643 376 children born in 2000-21 followed up for a median 9 years after birth in Sweden and 10 years in Norway and Denmark. INTERVENTIONS: Prenatal exposure, defined as ≥1 filled prescription for ADHD drug treatment anytime during pregnancy or in the second/third trimester (≥98 days after the last menstrual period).

makaleler.baslik_en: Licensing mechanisms during RNA-guided DNA integration by type I-F3 CAST.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Licensing mechanisms during RNA-guided DNA integration by type I-F3 CAST.
makaleler.ozet_en: Precise genomic integration of large DNA cargo remains a central challenge in genome engineering. CRISPR-associated transposases (CASTs)1,2 offer a promising solution by coupling RNA-guided DNA recognition to transposon-mediated integration. Because of their exceptional targeting fidelity, type I-F3 CASTs have been a major research focus1, yet the structural basis of their RNA-guided DNA integration has remained unclear. Here, using cryo-electron microscopy, computational protein design and functional assays, we report the licensing mechanisms that control DNA integration activity of Vibrio cholerae CAST (VchCAST).

makaleler.baslik_en: Performance of intracortical microelectrode arrays in people with implanted brain-computer interfaces over a 20-year period.
makaleler.baslik_tr: Performance of intracortical microelectrode arrays in people with implanted brain-computer interfaces over a 20-year period.
makaleler.ozet_en: The silicon microelectrode 'Utah' array has enabled people with paralysis to control computer cursors, operate prosthetic limbs and communicate using high-performance brain-computer interfaces. However, reports so far have typically been limited to one or two individuals, with no systematic assessment of array longevity, decoding accuracy and day-to-day stability. Here we present a comprehensive 20-year evaluation of neural data from the BrainGate clinical trials, spanning 2,289 recording sessions, 20 arrays and 14 participants.
